assertions.name: every character ratio lies in (0,1), so B = -alpha log R is positive
R = exp(-L) to the working floor — the character ratio IS the bond model
the hardcoded factor differs from the character ratio by more than 3x — it is a different object, not an approximation

description: Implements the character-ratio derivation path specified by prf:confined-knot-binding and admittedly not run by hecke_core_legacy.knot_factor. The character ratio nucleus/free-constituent-product, exact at 200 bits on the canonical word, equals exp(-L) to the working floor, so the specified path and the bond model are the same object. Binding from it: 2H +27.36 %, 3H -21.82 %, 3He -36.72 %, 4He -69.32 %. The hardcoded knot_factor (1-h^2 and its square) differs from the true character ratio by 4x to 7x and is not an approximation to it. Only the nucleon level is implemented; the quark and nuclear-jet levels the specification also names would push B up, which is a direction and not a prediction. No binding claim.
caveats: Nucleon level only. prf:confined-knot-binding names quark, nucleon and nuclear-jet levels; the exact engine has words for one of them.
No binding claim. That B = alpha L is the binding energy remains the open interpretation of rem:bond-log-ratio-is-a-free-energy.
Uses the canonical (chain) word. The all-pairs variant is not used because its bond multiset does not determine a word (qou-bygw, retired).
